title: the ACPI lens — what ships as bytes vs what gets built at runtime, and the DSDT clock
note: front C of ring 21: Q8's shipped-vs-built classification ported to the vendor corpus; admission is by ACPI CHECKSUM (a real table sums to 0 over its declared length), position only classifies the candidate; twelve specimens (nine ASUS rungs + three vendors)

validation_gates.gate: F67c ships DSDT+SSDT and generates FACP+APIC
10.41 Beta ships DSDT+SSDT and generates FACP+APIC

reading.q8_ported: the vendor mirror-vs-image boundary is the INVERSE of OVMF's: AMI ships the AML (DSDT variants + SSDTs, checksum-valid raw sections inside the compressed FV) and BUILDS every static table — zero FACP/APIC/MCFG/HPET/IVRS bytes anywhere in the images; OVMF builds all tables at runtime. The Q8 three-class model now has both sides measured
reading.the_factory_table_set: shared table bodies across all twelve boards: []

honesty: admission = checksum-valid table header; a corrupt-but-real table would be missed (the DSDT/SSDT admission passes on all twelve — and the whole-image debug scan found ZERO FACP bytes on 4655, so nothing was wrongly rejected)

the shipped set is AML only (DSDT+SSDT); FACP/APIC/MCFG/HPET/IVRS/XSDT are runtime-built by AMI's ACPI layer — the original gate expecting FACP to ship was the OVMF expectation, refuted by the bytes and rewritten
boards ship MULTIPLE distinct DSDT bodies (4 on every specimen here) — the DSDT clock takes the LARGEST body per rung; 'moves' means the main body changed, not that every variant did
OEM revision fields are read raw (integer); vendors are inconsistent about what increments them — the body hash is the honest movement signal
generator-class vocabulary (signature words inside PE bodies) is counted only when it never validates as a table anywhere in the image
